```{r}
############################################################
# M3A-1. Covariate data preparation and descriptive statistics
############################################################

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(readr)
library(here)

# 1. Read the cleaned modeling dataset
M3_data <- read_csv(
  here("Data", "warfarin_full_dataset_ID9_cleaned_for_popPKPD.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

# Check actual column names
names(M3_data)

# 2. Check whether baseline covariates are consistent within each ID
covariate_consistency <- M3_data %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  summarise(
    n_WT  = n_distinct(wt[!is.na(wt)]),
    n_AGE = n_distinct(age[!is.na(age)]),
    n_SEX = n_distinct(sex[!is.na(sex)]),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

inconsistent_ids <- covariate_consistency %>%
  filter(n_WT > 1 | n_AGE > 1 | n_SEX > 1)

inconsistent_ids

# 3. Create one subject-level covariate record per ID
cov_subject <- M3_data %>%
  select(id, wt, age, sex) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  arrange(id)

cov_subject

# 4. Continuous covariate summary
continuous_summary <- cov_subject %>%
  select(wt, age) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "covariate",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  group_by(covariate) %>%
  summarise(
    n       = sum(!is.na(value)),
    missing = sum(is.na(value)),
    mean    = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd      = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    median  = median(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    q1      = unname(quantile(value, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)),
    q3      = unname(quantile(value, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)),
    minimum = min(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    maximum = max(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    covariate = toupper(covariate),
    across(
      c(mean, sd, median, q1, q3, minimum, maximum),
      ~ round(.x, 2)
    )
  ) %>%
  as.data.frame()

continuous_summary

# 5. Categorical covariate summary
sex_summary <- cov_subject %>%
  mutate(
    sex = ifelse(
      is.na(sex),
      "Missing",
      as.character(sex)
    )
  ) %>%
  count(
    sex,
    name = "n",
    .drop = FALSE
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    percent = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)
  ) %>%
  rename(
    SEX = sex,
    N = n,
    Percent = percent
  ) %>%
  as.data.frame()

sex_summary

```

```{r}

############################################################
# M3A-2. Pearson correlation between WT and AGE
############################################################

library(dplyr)
library(tibble)

pearson_data <- cov_subject %>%
  transmute(
    id  = as.character(id),
    wt  = as.numeric(wt),
    age = as.numeric(age)
  ) %>%
  filter(
    complete.cases(wt, age)
  )

if (nrow(pearson_data) < 3) {
  stop("Fewer than three subjects have complete WT and AGE data.")
}

# Pearson correlation test for WT-AGE
pearson_test <- cor.test(
  x = pearson_data$wt,
  y = pearson_data$age,
  method = "pearson",
  conf.level = 0.95
)

# Report-ready result table
pearson_result <- tibble(
  Relationship = "WT vs AGE",
  N = nrow(pearson_data),
  Pearson_r = round(unname(pearson_test$estimate), 3),
  CI_lower = round(pearson_test$conf.int[1], 3),
  CI_upper = round(pearson_test$conf.int[2], 3),
  P_value = signif(pearson_test$p.value, 3)
)

pearson_result

# Scatter Plot for WT-AGE co-linearity

library(ggplot2)

pearson_subtitle <- sprintf(
  "Pearson r = %.3f; 95%% CI: %.3f to %.3f; N = %d",
  unname(pearson_test$estimate),
  pearson_test$conf.int[1],
  pearson_test$conf.int[2],
  nrow(pearson_data)
)

plot_wt_age <- ggplot(
  pearson_data,
  aes(x = wt, y = age)
) +
  geom_point(
    size = 2.5,
    alpha = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm",
    formula = y ~ x,
    se = TRUE
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    title = "Correlation Between Body Weight and Age",
    subtitle = pearson_subtitle,
    x = "Body Weight",
    y = "Age"
  )

plot_wt_age

```

```{r}
############################################################
# M3A-3. WT and AGE correlating to SEX
############################################################

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Prepare subject-level data
sex_plot_data <- cov_subject %>%
  mutate(
    wt = as.numeric(wt),
    age = as.numeric(age),
    sex_group = factor(sex)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(sex_group))


# WT-SEX Correlation

plot_wt_sex <- ggplot(
  sex_plot_data,
  aes(x = sex_group, y = wt)
) +
  geom_boxplot(
    outlier.shape = NA,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  geom_jitter(
    width = 0.10,
    height = 0,
    size = 2,
    alpha = 0.8,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    title = "Body Weight by Sex",
    x = "Sex group",
    y = "Body Weight"
  )

plot_wt_sex

# AGE-SEX Correlation

plot_age_sex <- ggplot(
  sex_plot_data,
  aes(x = sex_group, y = age)
) +
  geom_boxplot(
    outlier.shape = NA,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  geom_jitter(
    width = 0.10,
    height = 0,
    size = 2,
    alpha = 0.8,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    title = "Age by Sex",
    x = "Sex group",
    y = "Age"
  )

plot_age_sex
```

```{r}
############################################################
# M3A-4. ETA-covariate exploratory analysis
############################################################

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Organizing eta estimates from the selected base model in M2

fit_M3_base <- fit_M2_full_IIV    #YOU HAVE TO RUN M2 FIRST TO RUN THIS SECTION
fit_M3_data <- as.data.frame(fit_M3_base)
eta_subject <- fit_M3_data %>%
  transmute(
    id = as.character(ID),
    eta_cl = eta.cl,
    eta_v  = eta.v
  ) %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  summarise(
    eta_cl = first(eta_cl),
    eta_v  = first(eta_v),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Merge ETA estimates with the subject-level covariate dataset
eta_cov_data <- cov_subject %>%
  mutate(
    id = as.character(id),
    wt = as.numeric(wt),
    age = as.numeric(age),
    sex_group = factor(sex)
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    eta_subject,
    by = "id"
  )

eta_cov_data
```

```{r}
# ETA(CL/F) vs body weight
plot_eta_cl_wt <- ggplot(
  eta_cov_data,
  aes(x = wt, y = eta_cl)
) +
  geom_point(
    size = 2.5,
    alpha = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm",
    formula = y ~ x,
    se = TRUE
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    title = "ETA(CL/F) vs Body Weight",
    x = "Body Weight (kg)",
    y = "ETA(CL/F)"
  )

plot_eta_cl_wt
```
